title: The separated finitely presented etale site of a qcqs scheme
statement: Let $T$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Inside its small etale site $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $E(T)$ be the full category of objects $A\to T$ that are separated and of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Use small skeletons in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Then $E(T)$ contains $T\to T$, is closed under scheme-theoretic fibre products over any one of its objects [def-pc-fibre-product], and hence has finite limits computed in $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Every object of $E(T)$ is a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme. Finite jointly surjective families in $E(T)$ form a pretopology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; its associated topology is the topology induced from $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and restriction induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{Et}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(E(T))$ for sheaves of sets. For every morphism $e:T'\to T$ between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, scheme base change $A\mapsto A\times_TT'$ restricts to a functor $E(T)\to E(T')$ preserving finite limits and these finite covering families.

source.place: Tag 021D (lemma-fibre-products-etale) and Tag 04HR (lemma-alternative, comparison with the small affine etale site). Here the finite-limit-closed intermediate category is separated etale objects of finite presentation over a qcqs base, rather than only affine objects. The restriction uses schemes.tex lemmas separated-permanence and compose-after-separated, and morphisms.tex lemma-base-change-finite-presentation. This is the ordinary scheme-site input to ILO Expose XI, proof of Lemma 2.5 (printed p. 179).

proof.text: The identity $T\to T$ is etale, separated and of finite presentation directly from the definitions (its diagonal and all its affine restrictions are identities), and is terminal in the full subcategory $E(T)$. For $A\to T$ in $E(T)$, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $A$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. If $a:A\to C$ is a $T$-map between objects of $E(T)$, then $a$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation], applied to $A\to C\to T$. Its source is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and its target is quasi-separated, so clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Together with local finite presentation from etaleness, this says $a$ is of finite presentation.

For $A\to C\leftarrow B$ in $E(T)$, form $P=A\times_C B$. By step 1, $B\to C$ is separated and of finite presentation. Its base change $P\to A$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Compose with $A\to T$: clauses (d),(e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] give separated finite presentation of $P\to T$. The full-site finite-limit result [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] says it is etale and that this scheme fibre product is the full-site fibre product. Thus $P$ belongs to $E(T)$, and fullness gives its universal property there. The terminal object of step 1 and these pullbacks give all finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks]; the inclusion preserves them by the same result. Transport objects and limit cones to the selected small skeletons of [def-weil-size-convention]. All subsequent constructions may first be made before this transport.

Every full-site object $U\to T$ has an affine open cover: schemes are locally affine. For each affine open $W\subseteq U$, the map $W\to T$ is etale, since open immersions and composites of etale maps are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. It is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] and of finite presentation by the affine-source clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], since $T$ is quasi-separated. Thus these $W$ belong to $E(T)$ and cover $U$. More generally, given any full-site covering family $\{U_i\to A\}$ with $A\in E(T)$, take all affine opens $W\subseteq U_i$. They too belong to $E(T)$ and their maps to $A$ are etale by the same composition result. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] their images are open in $A$, and they cover $A$ because the original family is jointly surjective. Quasi-compactness of $A$ from step 1 selects finitely many such images. The corresponding affine maps give a finite jointly surjective family in $E(T)$ refining the original covering. This uses only the open-cover definition of quasi-compactness; for $A=\varnothing$ take the empty family.

source.place: Tag 04HR (lemma-alternative), proof by comparison with Tag 021E (lemma-affine-big-site-etale); schemes.tex Tags 01KN (lemma-affine-separated), 01KV (lemma-compose-after-separated).

proof.text: Let $\mathrm{Cov}$ consist of finite jointly surjective families with target and sources in $E(T)$. All arrows are etale by step 1. Isomorphism families are jointly surjective. A composite of two such covering families is again etale and jointly surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition], and its index set is a finite union of finite sets. Pulling back a family along any arrow of $E(T)$ stays inside $E(T)$ by step 2, and is etale and jointly surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]; the index set remains finite. These are the three pretopology axioms, including the empty cover of the empty scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition], its generated Grothendieck topology $J$ has the characterization: a sieve is $J$-covering exactly when it contains a family in $\mathrm{Cov}$.

source.place: Tags 0217 (lemma-etale) and 021C (lemma-verify-site-etale); sites.tex pretopology construction as recorded in lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition.

proof.text: Write $K$ for the full small etale topology and $i:E(T)\hookrightarrow T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. For a sieve $R$ on $A\in E(T)$, let $\overline{iR}$ be the full-site sieve generated by its arrows. If $R$ is $J$-covering, step 4 supplies a finite jointly surjective family in $R$, hence $\overline{iR}$ is $K$-covering by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition]. Conversely suppose $\overline{iR}$ is $K$-covering. The same pretopology characterization on the full site supplies an etale jointly surjective family $\{U_i\to A\}$ contained in $\overline{iR}$. Refine it by the finite affine covering $\{W_j\to A\}$ of step 3. Each $W_j\to A$ factors through some $U_i\to A$, and that arrow factors through a member $B\to A$ of $R$. Both $W_j$ and $B$ lie in $E(T)$, so the composite $W_j\to B$ is a morphism there by fullness; downward closure of $R$ gives $W_j\to A\in R$. Thus $R$ contains a family in $\mathrm{Cov}$ and is $J$-covering. This proves that $J$ is exactly the topology induced from $K$.

source.place: Tag 04HR (lemma-alternative), with the covering-refinement check of Tag 021E (lemma-affine-big-site-etale); sites.tex generated topology.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] to the fully faithful inclusion $i$ and the topologies $J,K$. Step 3 covers every full-site object by objects in the image, and step 5 verifies exactly its sieve criterion for the induced topology. The small skeletons fixed in step 2 make all comma categories in that lemma small; sets admit their limits. Its conclusion is precisely that restriction is an equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{Et}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(E(T))$ for sheaves of sets.

source.place: Tag 04HR (lemma-alternative) and sites.tex Tag 03A0 (lemma-equivalence), via the general dense-subsite comparison theorem.

proof.text: Let $e:T^{\prime}\to T$ be arbitrary with both bases qcqs. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], scheme base change is a functor on the full small etale sites and preserves their finite limits. By [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], it carries separated finite-presentation objects to separated finite-presentation objects. It therefore restricts to $E(T)\to E(T^{\prime})$. Since step 2 computes limits in both restricted categories as in their full sites, the restricted functor preserves finite limits. For a finite covering family its base change is etale and jointly surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], and finite with the same index set. These are exactly the required finite covering families. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or finite-type condition on $e$ was used.

Every cited statement node is a Mathlib leaf, so no tool_uses are needed and none were added. Step by step: (1) A is qcqs by permanence (2). A map a:A->C is étale by 02GW cancellation, separated by separated-cancellation (b), and qc/qs by permanence (1), so it is of finite presentation. (2) The fibre product P is separated and of finite presentation through base change, permanence (3) and proper-fp (d),(e). It is étale and a T_Et fibre product by etale-base-change-finite-limits (2). Terminal object plus pullbacks give all finite limits, and the inclusion preserves them. (3) Affine opens are étale (open immersion composed with étale), separated (affine source) and of finite presentation, which needs only T quasi-separated. A full-site cover of A in E(T) is refined by finitely many affine opens: images are open and A is quasi-compact. (4) The three pretopology axioms hold, using covering-composition, covering-base-change and pullbacks from step 2. (5) Both directions of the induced-sieve criterion hold: each W_j is an affine open inside some U_i, and fullness puts W_j->B in E(T). (6) The hypotheses of the dense-subsite equivalence match exactly, with small comma categories coming from the skeleton convention. (7) Base change along an arbitrary e between qcqs schemes preserves separated étale finite presentation, finite limits (computed in the full sites, inclusions fully faithful) and finite covers. Edge cases: T empty; T non-affine or non-separated; U_i not qc; e not qc; T=Spec k, which gives finite étale k-schemes. No duplicate in the DAG; related but distinct: etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings, finitary-site-coherent-generators and the affine-site comparison nodes. No fixes were made.
